notes:
Account summary
- Enterprise evaluation. Northbridge is an AI platform vendor; they embed LLM features into their own customer product and resell usage internally across multiple teams.
- Key theme: trust + transparency. They explicitly called out our status page and incident communications as part of procurement.

Primary stakeholders (Northbridge)
- Procurement lead (name redacted in CRM export)
- Security reviewer + platform engineering lead (name redacted)
- CS leader joined QBR follow-up focused on what Northbridge can forward to their end customers during incidents

What they’re building / workload
- Mix of chat + streaming UI (customer-facing), embeddings for retrieval, and reranking.
- They route across multiple models depending on tenant + latency budget; asked about routing/fallback policies and “graceful degradation” behaviors.
- Sensitivity: outages impacting streaming are treated differently than non-streaming generation failures (they want that reflected publicly).

Requirements (noted during evaluation)
- Status page:
  - Wants component split by capability and region (example they gave: “Streaming (US-East) Degraded” vs “Hosted API (EU-West) Operational”).
  - Wants embeddings called out separately from general API health (“status page says API ok but embeddings failing” is a recurring pain point for them with other vendors).
  - Asked whether we can represent partial impact / degraded performance without calling it a full outage.
- Incident comms:
  - Asked for documented Time To First Update target (they used language like “<30 min preferred” but also asked what we can realistically commit to).
  - Wants standard cadence guidance for ongoing incidents (e.g., every 30–60 min) and a clear “who approves updates” answer for high severity.
  - Wants templates they can forward internally (investigating / identified / mitigating / monitoring / resolved).
- Post-incident summaries:
  - Strong request for consistent, publishable post-incident summary format. Quote from call: “We need something we can send to our customers without redactions.”
  - Requested: impact window, customer impact description, root cause class (ok if high-level), mitigation, and prevention/follow-ups.
  - They asked for timing expectation (they asked for 3–5 business days; we said we’re standardizing and will confirm policy).
- Security/compliance:
  - VPC/private deployment preferred for production; hosted ok for POC.
  - SSO/SAML required for Console access; audit logs and retention controls required.
  - Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU (processing + logs). KMS integration expected.

Timeline / activity log
- 2025-11-06 (Fireflies): procurement call focused on incident comms + status page expectations. They asked for examples of “good incident updates” and whether we publish retro links.
- 2025-11-10: internal approval to proceed with status page transparency upgrades plan (used to inform what we can share externally).
- 2025-11-14 (Fireflies): CS/QBR follow-up. Northbridge reiterated they need per-region components and publishable summaries; asked if Console can link to incident summaries.
- 2025-11-20 (Fireflies): security review. Asked: how incidents are declared, what triggers a public incident, how approval works for Sev0/Sev1 updates, and what’s included/excluded in public summaries.

Open questions / risks
- Need to align on what we can commit to for comms SLAs vs best-effort (avoid over-promising). They will treat this as contractual language.
- Dedicated/Private visibility: they asked if their dedicated cluster incidents show on public status page or a separate customer-scoped view (we need consistent guidance).

Internal action items
- Provide Northbridge a customer-facing explainer:
  - Status page component definitions + how regions/capabilities map
  - Incident update phases + example wording
  - Post-incident summary example (sanitized)
- Confirm policy: publishable post-incident summary timing + approval chain (loop in Legal/Security for wording constraints).
- SE to propose POC architecture (hosted for dev + VPC/private for prod), with region plan US-East + EU-West.

Deal notes
- Northbridge is comparing vendors on operational maturity as much as raw model performance.
- They explicitly said: “If we can’t trust the status page, our support org gets crushed.”
- Likely expansion if we can satisfy comms + transparency requirements; initial footprint moderate but strategic logo.
